title: 蟹 逅 伦 敦！

sentences.zh: 伦敦有一只非常著名的小熊，就是帕丁顿熊。
sentences.en: There's a famous little bear in London, Paddington Bear.
sentences.note: 开场介绍：There's a…（比 There is 更口语），famous little bear（little 增加亲切感，不是 small）

sentences.zh: 他是从很远的秘鲁坐船过来的。
sentences.en: He came all the way from Peru by boat.
sentences.note: 大老远过来 → all the way from…（强调距离之远，口语高频）；坐船 → by boat

sentences.zh: 我觉得我跟他特别的像，也是从大老远的地方坐飞机过来的。
sentences.en: I feel like I'm a lot like him, I also came from far away, but by plane.
sentences.note: 很像他 → a lot like him（比 very similar to 更自然）；大老远 → far away（不必直译 big old far）

sentences.zh: 但我大概不是果酱，带的是一箱子的设备。
sentences.en: Instead of marmalade, I brought a suitcase full of gear.
sentences.note: 果酱 → marmalade（英式橙皮果酱，帕丁顿熊最爱，不是 jam）；一箱 → a suitcase full of；设备 → gear（泛指拍摄设备）

sentences.zh: 帕丁顿来到伦敦时，脖子上挂着一张写着「请照顾好这只熊」的纸条。
sentences.en: When Paddington arrived in London, he had a tag around his neck that said "please look after this bear."
sentences.note: 纸条 → tag（行李牌/标签，不是 note/paper）；照顾 → look after（英式表达，比 take care of 更常用）；脖子上挂着 → had a tag around his neck

sentences.zh: 第一次来到伦敦的我也想借用一下这句话：请照顾好这只蟹。
sentences.en: As a first-timer in London, I'd like to borrow that line: please look after this crab.
sentences.note: 第一次来的人 → first-timer（口语名词）；借用这句话 → borrow that line（比 use that sentence 更自然）

sentences.zh: 在真正站在这里之前，我对伦敦的认识其实还蛮零碎的。
sentences.en: Before standing here, my knowledge of London was pretty scattered.
sentences.note: 零碎的 → scattered（比 fragmented/piecemeal 更口语）；蛮…的 → pretty…（口语缓冲词）

sentences.zh: 大本钟、阴晴不定的天气，还有电影里那些似曾相识的街道。
sentences.en: Big Ben, unpredictable weather, and streets that felt familiar from movies.
sentences.note: 阴晴不定 → unpredictable（不是 cloudy-sunny）；似曾相识 → felt familiar from…（feel familiar 更地道，比 looked familiar 更主观）

sentences.zh: 所以这一次我想认真当一回游客，也想看看那些电影里的地方现实中到底是什么样的。
sentences.en: So this time I want to be a proper tourist and see what those movie locations actually look like in real life.
sentences.note: 认真当游客 → proper tourist（proper = 货真价实的、合格的）；电影取景地 → movie locations；现实中 → in real life

sentences.zh: 欢迎收看本期的邂逅时间——伦敦。
sentences.en: Welcome to this episode of Encounter Time, London.
sentences.note: 本期 → this episode（视频/vlog 专用）；邂逅 → encounter（通识词，比 chance meeting 简洁）

paraphrase.label: 大老远过来
paraphrase.en: all the way from Peru. / all the way over from China. / from as far away as...

paraphrase.label: 带着设备而非果酱
paraphrase.en: Instead of marmalade, I brought a suitcase full of gear.

paraphrase.label: 借用这句话
paraphrase.en: borrow that line / steal that line / let me quote that

paraphrase.label: 认真当一回游客
paraphrase.en: be a proper tourist / do the whole tourist thing / play tourist for real

scenes.title_cn: 初到伦敦：大本钟与天气

sentences.zh: 家人们到伦敦了！
sentences.en: Hey guys, we made it to London.
sentences.note: 到了 → made it（比 arrived 更口语，含「终于到了」的成就感）；家人们 → guys（Vlog 通用称呼，不是 family members）

sentences.zh: 既然是第一次来，那有些游客作业总还是要交一下的。后面是大本钟。
sentences.en: Since it's my first time, I gotta do the obligatory tourist stuff. Big Ben is right behind me.
sentences.note: 游客作业 → obligatory tourist stuff（obligatory = 必须打卡的，比 must-do 更具体）；就在后面 → right behind me（right 强调方位）

sentences.zh: 但今天一到伦敦这个天气就非常典型，特别的伦敦——阴雨绵绵的。
sentences.en: But the weather today is just so typical, so London, drizzly and grey.
sentences.note: 特别伦敦 → so London（名词当形容词用，地道口语）；阴雨绵绵 → drizzly and grey（drizzle = 毛毛雨）

sentences.zh: 但是据说其实伦敦全年的降雨量没有上海多，这个你改心。
sentences.en: Apparently London's annual rainfall is actually less than Shanghai's, let that sink in.
sentences.note: 全年降雨量 → annual rainfall；你想想 → let that sink in（「细品一下」的高频说法，比 think about it 更有冲击力）

sentences.zh: 主要是它每次都是下一点点毛毛雨。可能这就是为什么经常看到伦敦人下雨天不打伞的原因吧。
sentences.en: It's mainly because it's always just a light drizzle. Maybe that's why you often see Londoners not bothering with umbrellas.
sentences.note: 毛毛雨 → light drizzle；懒得打伞 → not bothering with umbrellas（bother = 费那个劲、麻烦，比 don't use umbrellas 更传神）

paraphrase.label: 到了某地
paraphrase.en: We made it to London! / We're here! / Touchdown London!

paraphrase.label: 必须打卡的游客项目
paraphrase.en: the obligatory tourist stuff / the must-do tourist checklist / the standard tourist routine

paraphrase.label: 典型伦敦天气
paraphrase.en: so typical, so London / classic London / peak London / couldn't be more London

sentences.zh: 我后面这个墙上全都是爱心。
sentences.en: The wall behind me is covered in hearts.
sentences.note: 全是爱心 → covered in hearts（covered in = 被…覆盖，比 full of 更有画面感）

sentences.zh: 但这里每颗爱心都代表一位新冠逝者。
sentences.en: But each heart here represents someone who passed away from COVID.
sentences.note: 代表 → represents（不是 means）；逝者 → someone who passed away（passed away 比 died 更委婉）

paraphrase.label: 墙上全是…
paraphrase.en: covered in hearts / plastered with hearts / full of hearts

paraphrase.label: 因新冠去世
paraphrase.en: passed away from COVID / died of COVID / lost their life to COVID

scenes.title_cn: 落地第一顿：炸鱼薯条 & 中餐

sentences.zh: 落地伦敦的第一顿当然要吃炸鱼薯条了。
sentences.en: For my first meal in London, fish and chips was a no-brainer.
sentences.note: 落地第一顿 → first meal in London；理所当然的选择 → a no-brainer（比 an obvious choice 更口语）

sentences.zh: 我们找到一家从1988年开到现在、号称英国顶尖的老店。
sentences.en: We found a place that's been around since 1988, supposedly one of the best in the UK.
sentences.note: 开到现在 → been around since（比 been open since 更口语）；号称 → supposedly（暗示「据说是，但不确定」）

sentences.zh: 还碰到一个当地人跟我们说这是伦敦最好吃的炸鱼薯条。
sentences.en: Even ran into a local who told us it's the best fish and chips in London.
sentences.note: 碰到某人 → ran into（偶遇，比 met 更口语）；当地人 → a local（名词，非常常用）

sentences.zh: 最好吃不敢说，但伦敦第一顿的仪式感算是有了。
sentences.en: Can't say if it's the best, but at least we got that first-meal-in-London ritual out of the way.
sentences.note: 不敢说 → can't say if…（比 I'm not sure 更口语）；仪式感有了 → got that ritual out of the way（解除仪式负担，比 completed the ritual 更地道）

sentences.zh: 仪式归仪式，但中国胃是不一样的。所以我们来了一家从某个年代开到现在的老店。
sentences.en: Rituals aside, a Chinese stomach is a different story. So we came to this long-standing spot.
sentences.note: 仪式归仪式 → rituals aside（aside = 暂且不论）；中国胃 → a Chinese stomach（直译即可，英语完全理解这个文化概念）；是另一回事 → is a different story

sentences.zh: 来看看这个西安的肉夹馍，折算下来一百多块钱一份。
sentences.en: Check out this Xi'an-style roujiamo, works out to over a hundred yuan each.
sentences.note: 换来 → check out（Vlog 展示用语）；折算下来 → works out to（换算/结果，高频口语）

sentences.zh: 中餐出了国，价格是涨了，魅力倒是一点没打折。
sentences.en: Chinese food abroad, the price goes up, but the appeal doesn't drop one bit.
sentences.note: 魅力 → appeal（比 charm 更中性，适用于食物）；一点没打折扣 → doesn't drop one bit（口语强调，比 doesn't decrease at all 更有力）

paraphrase.label: 理所当然的选择
paraphrase.en: a no-brainer / an obvious choice / goes without saying

paraphrase.label: 仪式感完成了
paraphrase.en: got that ritual out of the way / checked that box / ticked that off the list

paraphrase.label: 中餐出国：价格涨了魅力不减
paraphrase.en: the price goes up, but the appeal doesn't drop one bit / still just as good / every bit as tempting

paraphrase.label: 折算下来
paraphrase.en: works out to / comes to / adds up to / that's about

sentences.zh: 伦敦还有一家挺有名的酒吧，但是我没有预约，最后只能坐在了吧台位。
sentences.en: There's this pretty famous bar in London, but I didn't have a reservation, so I ended up at the counter.
sentences.note: 挺有名的 → pretty famous（pretty 作副词 = 相当）；最后只能 → ended up at（结果落在了，口语高频）

sentences.zh: 但是没有想到这个临时的座位真的是全场景佳的景观位。
sentences.en: But who would've thought, this last-minute seat turned out to be the best view in the whole place.
sentences.note: 没想到 → who would've thought（修辞反问，比 surprisingly 更口语）；临时座位 → last-minute seat；竟然是 → turned out to be

sentences.zh: 怎么样，体验感拉满吧？不过账单也一样。
sentences.en: Pretty amazing experience, right? Though the bill was just as impressive.
sentences.note: 体验感拉满 → amazing experience（比 off the charts 更简洁）；账单也一样 → the bill was just as impressive（just as = 和体验一样令人印象深刻）

paraphrase.label: 结果却坐了吧台
paraphrase.en: I ended up at the counter / I wound up at the bar / I had to settle for the bar seat

paraphrase.label: 没想到却是最佳位置
paraphrase.en: who would've thought it turned out to be the best view / turns out / surprisingly enough

paraphrase.label: 体验感拉满
paraphrase.en: a top-tier experience / the experience was off the charts / couldn't have asked for more

sentences.zh: 虽然伦敦是第一次来，但有些画面早就在电影里面见过了。
sentences.en: Even though it's my first time in London, some of these scenes I've already seen in movies.
sentences.note: 画面 → scenes（不是 pictures/images）；在电影里见过 → seen in movies（最简单直接）

sentences.zh: 比如眼前的这个帕丁顿车站，是不是还挺熟悉的？
sentences.en: Like Paddington Station right here, does it look familiar?
sentences.note: 是不是挺眼熟 → does it look familiar?（口语反问，比 don't you recognize it 更自然）

sentences.zh: 今天我们就拿电影当地图，看看银幕外的伦敦。
sentences.en: Today we're using movies as our map to see London beyond the screen.
sentences.note: 拿电影当地图 → using movies as our map（as = 当作）；银幕外 → beyond the screen（比 outside the movie 更优雅）

sentences.zh: 跟随着帕丁顿熊的足迹，我来到了英国的自然历史博物馆，这里就是帕丁顿熊差点被抓起做成标本的地方。
sentences.en: Following Paddington's footsteps, I ended up at the Natural History Museum, the very place where Paddington was almost turned into a stuffed specimen.
sentences.note: 足迹 → footsteps；正是那个地方 → the very place where（very 表示强调=正是）；做成标本 → turned into a stuffed specimen

sentences.zh: 哇这里真的好壮观！挑高非常的高，像一个城堡一样。
sentences.en: Wow this place is absolutely stunning, the ceiling is so high, it's like a castle.
sentences.note: 壮观 → stunning（比 magnificent 更口语）；挑高 → the ceiling is so high（ceiling = 天花板高度即挑高）；像城堡 → like a castle

sentences.zh: 这个大厅里面最值得看的就是这个被吊起来的蓝鲸化石。
sentences.en: The main thing to see in this hall is the blue whale skeleton hanging from the ceiling.
sentences.note: 最值得看 → the main thing to see（比 the most worth seeing 更自然）；蓝鲸化石 → blue whale skeleton；吊起来 → hanging from the ceiling

sentences.zh: 它整个动作就是一个向下俯冲捕食的动作，我感觉站在它下面特别的小。
sentences.en: It's posed mid-dive, like it's swooping down to catch prey. I feel so tiny standing underneath it.
sentences.note: 定格在俯冲动作 → posed mid-dive（mid- = 在半空中/过程中）；俯冲捕食 → swooping down to catch prey；特别小 → so tiny（比 very small 更有冲击力）

sentences.zh: 这些化石看着确实挺震撼的，但这里还有很多动物标本，真的每一只都栩栩如生。
sentences.en: The fossils are genuinely impressive, but there are also loads of animal specimens here, every single one looks so lifelike.
sentences.note: 震撼 → genuinely impressive（genuinely = 真的，不是夸张）；很多 → loads of（英式口语，比 many 更自然）；栩栩如生 → lifelike（比 vivid 更贴标本语境）

sentences.zh: 能近距离看到这么多难得一见的标本，确实挺厉害的。
sentences.en: Getting to see so many rare specimens up close is pretty amazing.
sentences.note: 近距离 → up close（比 at a close distance 更简洁）；难得一见的 → rare（比 hard to see 更简洁）

sentences.zh: 只是关于它们生前的故事咱就不了解了。希望它们都是在生命结束以后才以这种方式被留在这里的。
sentences.en: Though I don't really know the stories of how they lived. I just hope they ended up here after their lives ran their natural course.
sentences.note: 生前故事 → the stories of how they lived；生命自然终结后 → after their lives ran their natural course（委婉表达「不是被杀死做标本」，比 after a natural death 更优美）

paraphrase.label: 银幕外
paraphrase.en: beyond the screen / off-screen / the real thing / in real life

paraphrase.label: 跟随某人的足迹
paraphrase.en: following someone's footsteps / retracing someone's steps / walking in someone's path

paraphrase.label: 特别小
paraphrase.en: so tiny / feel dwarfed / feel puny / feel so small

paraphrase.label: 栩栩如生
paraphrase.en: lifelike / so realistic / true to life / uncannily real

sentences.zh: 不知道有多少人是先看了《诺丁山》，后来才知道伦敦真的有这个地方叫诺丁山。
sentences.en: I wonder how many people watched Notting Hill first and only later found out it's an actual place in London.
sentences.note: 不知道有多少人 → I wonder how many people…（wonder = 好奇/想知道）；后来才知道 → only later found out（found out = 发现/得知）

sentences.zh: 电影里那间小小的旅行书店，也成了很多人记住这里的原因。
sentences.en: That tiny travel bookshop in the movie is what made this place stick in so many people's minds.
sentences.note: 旅行书店 → travel bookshop（不是 travel bookstore，英式用法）；记住这里 → stick in people's minds（stick = 留在记忆里，比 remember 更形象）

sentences.zh: 这就是电影中男女主角相遇的142号店，但实际上它并不是一家书店，而是一个纪念品商店。
sentences.en: This is number 142, where the leads meet in the film, but it's not actually a bookshop, it's a souvenir store.
sentences.note: 男女主角 → the leads（主演的简称，比 the main characters 更专业）；纪念品商店 → souvenir store

sentences.zh: 实际上电影中书店的灵感是来自有生活的这家书店，但有意思的是这里其实也没有真的拍过电影。剧组只是照着当时的书店在摄影棚里重新搭了一间。
sentences.en: The real-life inspiration for the bookshop was actually this other bookstore, but funnily enough, they never filmed there either. The crew just built a replica of it on a soundstage.
sentences.note: 灵感来源 → the real-life inspiration；有意思的是 → funnily enough（英式口语）；照原样搭了一间 → built a replica；摄影棚 → on a soundstage

sentences.zh: 你看电影不一定是真的，但它确实能让一条街变成让全世界人都来打卡的地方——这个倒是真的。
sentences.en: Movies may not be real, but they can definitely turn a street into a place people from all over the world come to check out, that part is very real.
sentences.note: 打卡 → come to check out（比 take photos 更贴旅行打卡含义）；这个倒是真的 → that part is very real（精妙转折，呼应前句的 not real）

paraphrase.label: 后来才发现
paraphrase.en: only later found out / it wasn't until later that I realized / only discovered afterwards

paraphrase.label: 留在记忆里
paraphrase.en: stick in someone's mind / make an impression / leave a mark / be etched in memory

paraphrase.label: 有意思的是
paraphrase.en: funnily enough / ironically / the funny thing is / here's the twist

sentences.zh: 这里就是伦敦的裁缝街，有的店铺已经开了几百年了。
sentences.en: This is Savile Row, some of these shops have been around for centuries.
sentences.note: 裁缝街 → Savile Row（专有名词，不用翻译）；开了几百年 → been around for centuries（been around = 一直存在）

sentences.zh: 听说这边一套定制西装要几千英镑，要等六个星期。
sentences.en: I heard a bespoke suit here costs a few thousand pounds and takes six weeks.
sentences.note: 定制西装 → bespoke suit（bespoke = 量身定做，英式核心词汇，不是 custom-made）；几千英镑 → a few thousand pounds（pounds 不要省略）

sentences.zh: 不过让这条街出圈的不只是西装，而是一部叫 Kingsman 的电影。
sentences.en: But what really put this street on the map wasn't just the suits, it was a movie called Kingsman.
sentences.note: 出圈/出名 → put this street on the map（经典习语，比 make it famous 更地道）

sentences.zh: 你看这写的 Kingsman。这家店是1849年的时候开的。
sentences.en: See it says Kingsman right here. This shop first opened in 1849.
sentences.note: 你看 → See（Vlog 引导观众看画面）；这写着 → it says… right here（right here 强调当前画面）

sentences.zh: 据说当时《王牌特工》的导演就是在这里量体裁衣的时候突然来了灵感，于是就拍了这部电影。
sentences.en: Apparently the director of Kingsman was here getting fitted when inspiration struck, and that's how the movie was born.
sentences.note: 量体裁衣 → getting fitted（西装量体的固定说法）；突然来了灵感 → inspiration struck（strike = 突然降临，比 got inspiration 更生动）

sentences.zh: 来看看这件西装的价格。好贵，两万多。
sentences.en: Let's take a look at the price of this suit. So expensive, over twenty thousand.
sentences.note: 来看看 → let's take a look at（Vlog 引导句式）；好贵 → so expensive（夸张脱口而出，比 very expensive 更口语）

sentences.zh: 走进去之后才发现它们写了不让我们拍摄，但我还是偷偷摸摸拍了一点。好像也没有制止我，整个偷感非常重。
sentences.en: After walking in, I noticed a sign saying no filming, but I still snuck in a few shots. They didn't seem to stop me either, so the whole thing felt super sneaky.
sentences.note: 写着不让拍 → a sign saying no filming；偷偷摸摸拍了 → snuck in a few shots（snuck = sneak 过去式，偷偷做）；偷感重 → super sneaky（sneaky = 鬼鬼祟祟的）

sentences.zh: 我悄悄看了一下，它里面的衣服价格还蛮高的，要两千多磅一件。就是普通黑色的西装，可能只是我看不出它的特别之处。
sentences.en: I took a quiet look, the prices inside are pretty steep, over two thousand pounds a piece. It was just a plain black suit, maybe I just can't tell what makes it special.
sentences.note: 价格蛮高 → pretty steep（steep = 价格高得吓人）；一件 → a piece（服装量词）；看不出特别之处 → can't tell what makes it special（比 can't see why it's special 更自然）

sentences.zh: 不过这地方特别有名，像很多英国的政要，比如丘吉尔、威廉王子，都在这边定制过西装。
sentences.en: But this place is seriously famous, loads of British figures like Churchill and Prince William have had suits made here.
sentences.note: 政要 → British figures（figures = 重要人物，比 politicians 更宽泛）；定制过西装 → have had suits made here（have something done 句型，意为让别人给自己做）

paraphrase.label: 让这里出名
paraphrase.en: put this street on the map / made this street famous / put this street in the spotlight

paraphrase.label: 突然来了灵感
paraphrase.en: inspiration struck / he got the idea / a lightbulb went off / it hit him

paraphrase.label: 偷偷拍了
paraphrase.en: snuck in a few shots / secretly filmed a bit / got some sneaky footage / stole a few clips

paraphrase.label: 价格很高
paraphrase.en: pretty steep / pretty pricey / on the expensive side / not cheap at all

sentences.zh: 在伦敦的这几天，雨就没怎么停过，但到了最后一天——哎，天晴了。
sentences.en: The rain barely let up during my days in London, but on the final day, hey, the sun came out.
sentences.note: 没怎么停过 → barely let up（let up = 减弱/停止，高频天气表达）；天晴了 → the sun came out（比 it stopped raining 更有画面感）

sentences.zh: 大本钟还是那个大本钟，可太阳一出来，看起来就像换了一座城市。
sentences.en: Big Ben is still Big Ben, but when the sun comes out, it feels like a whole different city.
sentences.note: 还是那个大本钟 → Big Ben is still Big Ben（修辞重复，不变的是标志建筑）；像换了个城市 → a whole different city（whole = 完全，强调反差之大）

sentences.zh: 至于伦敦到底是什么样，我第一次来确实说不太清。
sentences.en: As for what London is really like, honestly, I can't quite put my finger on it after just one visit.
sentences.note: 说不太清 → can't quite put my finger on it（经典习语 = 无法准确描述/指出，比 can't describe it 更地道）

sentences.zh: 电影里的那些地方算是找到了，但电影之外的伦敦可能还得再来几次。
sentences.en: I managed to find all those movie locations, but the London beyond the movies? Might take a few more trips.
sentences.note: 总算找到了 → managed to find（managed to = 经过努力做到了）；电影之外的伦敦 → the London beyond the movies（beyond 呼应开头的 beyond the screen）；还得再来 → might take a few more trips

sentences.zh: 当然也欢迎屏幕前的你来分享一下，你眼中的伦敦是什么样子。
sentences.en: And of course, I'd love for you guys to share, what does London look like through your eyes?
sentences.note: 欢迎你分享 → I'd love for you guys to share（Vlog 结尾互动句）；你眼中 → through your eyes（比 in your opinion 更形象诗意）

paraphrase.label: 雨没停过
paraphrase.en: barely let up / hardly stopped / almost never let up / was pretty much nonstop

paraphrase.label: 说不太清
paraphrase.en: can't quite put my finger on it / can't really pin it down / hard to sum up

paraphrase.label: 总算做到了
paraphrase.en: managed to find / was able to track down / did get to see / checked off

practice.zh: 用「made it / all the way from」表达「终于到了、从很远的地方来」
practice.en: We made it to London! I came all the way from China for this.

practice.zh: 用「ended up at… / turned out to be…」表达意料之外的结果
practice.en: I ended up at the counter, but it turned out to be the best seat in the house.

practice.zh: 用「put… on the map」表达「让某地出名」
practice.en: That one movie put this tiny street on the map for tourists around the world.

practice.zh: 用「can't quite put my finger on it」表达「说不清楚、无法准确描述」
practice.en: I can't quite put my finger on what makes this city so special, but I love it.
